text: A Failover Cluster Instance is built on the same clustering technology as Availability Groups, but solves HA at a different level — the entire SQL Server instance fails over as one unit, not per-database.

An AG fails over a named group of databases, each replica with its own copy. An FCI fails over the whole instance, every node sharing one copy on the same disk. Only which node owns the shared storage actually changes.
A DBA reaches for FCI when whole-instance protection is simpler than many AGs, when shared storage already exists, or when Standard Edition licensing rules out full Availability Groups.
The shared storage itself becomes the single point of failure that matters most, which is why FCI is often paired with an AG spanning separate FCIs. Next up: Active Geo-Replication.
